mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as capital flows into risk assets.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical correlation between FEDFUNDS < 0.25% and positive 20d SPX returns
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rates exceeding 5.0% signal deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP (GDPC1) indicates robust consumer demand, driving corporate revenue and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST and GDPC1 growth correlate with 20d SPX gains
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and GDPC1 fails to produce positive returns in > 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during inflationary regimes.
evidence_refs: fact:CPIAUCSL > 3.0 historically correlates with negative 20d SPX returns
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production (INDPRO > 100.0) reflects robust manufacturing activity, boosting corporate output and profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth above 100.0 fails to generate positive returns in > 50% of 60-day windows over a 3-year rolling period.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating employment growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) signals improving labor market conditions, increasing consumer spending and corporate revenue, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly correlates with 5d SPX gains
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer spending and housing demand, driving corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:RSAFS and HOUST growth have positive joint correlation with equity returns
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising RSAFS and HOUST fails to produce positive returns in > 50% of instances over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening signaled by FEDFUNDS > 2.0% increases borrowing costs and reduces liquidity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during tightening cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0% over a 3-year rolling window.
